findings.text: Inverted condition: default packages are installed only when EXIT_CODE indicates failure (-ne 0) instead of success. With a successful nvm use and NVM_UPGRADE_NPM=1, EXIT_CODE=0 causes the condition to fail, skipping default package installation entirely.
Inverted condition: reinstall-packages only runs when EXIT_CODE indicates failure (-ne 0). A successful installation with EXIT_CODE=0 will skip reinstalling packages from the previous version.
Inverted condition: alias is only set when EXIT_CODE indicates failure (-ne 0). A successful install with EXIT_CODE=0 will not create the requested alias.

EXIT_CODE may be uninitialized when NVM_UPGRADE_NPM is not set to 1. The variable is only assigned inside the NVM_UPGRADE_NPM=1 block, but used in conditions at lines 43, 48, and 59, causing unpredictable behavior.

EXIT_CODE may be uninitialized in the fresh install path if nvm use is not called or fails silently. The condition [ $EXIT_CODE -eq 0 ] at line 79 would then behave unpredictably, potentially skipping default package installation.

3.reason: EXIT_CODE is uninitialized in the already-installed path when NVM_UPGRADE_NPM is not 1, and the inverted conditions at lines 43/48/59 (the gating on [ $EXIT_CODE -ne 0 ]) are the same root cause as the reference bug.

4.reason: The fresh install path's EXIT_CODE is uninitialized if nvm use is not called or fails silently, and the condition [ $EXIT_CODE -eq 0 ] at line 79 is the same inverted-test mechanism as the reference bug, causing default packages to be skipped.
